prior.text: Decide the policy: after how many consecutive failures on the same offset is a batch skipped, and is a durable 4xx distinguished from a transient error by status code rather than by count

entry.text: Decide the policy: after how many consecutive failures on the same offset is a batch skipped, and is a durable 4xx distinguished from a transient error by status code rather than by count
entry.evidence: 4671ba0fd — CloudLogUploadFailurePolicy.action(for:): decided by status code, not by count. rejectRows for any 4xx except 401/403/404/408/429, and for .encoding; retryLater for 5xx, transport and the auth/not-found/timeout/rate-limit 4xx. A rejected range bisects down to the one row and drops it.

prior.text: Skipping emits telemetry naming what was dropped (offset range, line count, last status), so a silent skip can never look like a successful drain

entry.text: Skipping emits telemetry naming what was dropped (offset range, line count, last status), so a silent skip can never look like a successful drain
entry.evidence: 4671ba0fd — each drop uploads CloudLogEvent.rowDropped: event=cloud_log_row_dropped status=<code|encoding> rows=<1+lostSkips> range=<segment:offset>..<segment:offset> (category CloudLogging, warn), straight through the provider (not CloudLogSink/TrioLogger), and it counts against the request budget. prior.text: Consecutive-failure state is durable, not in-memory — a relaunch must not reset the counter and re-stall on the same batch

entry.text: Consecutive-failure state is durable, not in-memory — a relaunch must not reset the counter and re-stall on the same batch
entry.evidence: 4671ba0fd — no counter: the decision comes from the status code, so the state lives only in the queue cursor, which is already durable. After a relaunch the same row gets the same 4xx and is dropped in the same pass, and nothing in memory can reset and re-stall it.
